topic: A Fridge Doesn't Make Cold, It Moves Heat Out
creativeBrief:

Generate five declarative, concrete subject-first hooks; prefer 6-10 words and do not give away the mechanism at once. Six story functions across five voiced scenes of 6 seconds each: visual paradox, contradiction, clue, mechanism, distinct second reveal, payoff. The opening frame shows the object already moving. Start the mechanism about 5 seconds in, at the clue scene. YouTube title seed: Why Is the Back of Your Fridge Warm?
YouTube description seed: Put your hand near the back or sides of your fridge. Warm? Guess where that heat came from. #TellMeWhyyyyyy #Shorts
The central fact: A fridge pulls heat out of the food and dumps it into your kitchen through the coils.
The later surprise: The heat out the back is more than the heat taken from inside, because the compressor adds its own.
The very first frame shows a hand moving slowly along the back of a fridge in a bright home kitchen, hovering near the black condenser coils as warm air shimmers above them. It is already moving in the first frame, and nothing in the first second gives the answer away.
What changes inside each 6s clip:
Scene 1 (contradiction, 0-6s): Opening: the hand already moving along the warm coils. About 2s in, the hand pulls back slightly from the heat; about 4s in, the fridge door on the other side opens to cold air.
Scene 2 (clue, 6-12s): Mechanism starts about 5s in. Inside the fridge, frost on the real evaporator panel at the back wall; about 2-3s later, a thermometer inside reads cold; then a matching thermometer near the back coils reads warm.
Scene 3 (mechanism, 12-18s): A real refrigerant circuit on a service-training bench (real parts or physical props only, no animation or cutaway graphics) with evaporator, compressor and condenser in view; about 2s in, a finger traces the pipe from the cold coil to the compressor; about 4s in, it traces on to the condenser.
Scene 4 (second_reveal, 18-24s): The compressor at the bottom rear humming; about 2s in, a hand hovers near its housing; about 4s in, warm air rises from the condenser coils.
Scene 5 (payoff, 24-30s): Narration states that the coils release both the heat pumped out of the food and the heat from the compressor's own work. Cold drinks come out of the fridge; about 2s in, the hand moves back toward the warm coils; about 4s in, return to the exact opening: the same hand moving along the same warm coils at the back of the same fridge, same framing as scene 1's first frame, so it loops.
Fact boundaries: Condenser location varies by model; do not say every fridge has coils on the back. Do not suggest touching hot or moving parts, unplugging, or opening the sealed system. Do not claim specific energy savings.

facts.statement: Inside the fridge, a very cold liquid called refrigerant flows through the evaporator coil, soaks up heat from the food and air, and evaporates into a gas.
The compressor squeezes that gas into a hot, high-pressure gas and pushes it into the condenser coil outside the cold compartment.
In the condenser coil the gas gives its heat to the kitchen air and turns back into a liquid; the heat let out there is the heat taken from inside plus the heat from the compressor's work.
